notes: The action registry: every verb the agent can dispatch is defined once here.
It is language neutral. The TypeScript code (src/background/agent/actions.ts and schemas.ts) reads it with an import, and the Python runner will read the same file.
verbs is in prompt order. A verb is a page verb (the content script or the background runs it on the page) or a state verb (it changes the run, not the page).

tiers says which model tiers may use the verb. modes says which policy modes offer it, as listed in the design (docs/langgraph-design.md, Policy modes). State verbs that arrive later (record_finding, mark_blocked, ...) are added to this list with their modes.
prompt is the exact line of the compact Ollama prompt, the field list included. A test keeps the field list equal to schema.properties.

schema is the decoding branch of the verb. The builder adds the const action, additionalProperties:false, and an optional reason string (unless it is switched off). required lists the fields the model must always send, because small models fill required fields and drop optional ones.
In a property, {"$ref": "#/$defs/name"} is replaced by that entry of $defs, and {"$batchSteps": true} by the browser_batch steps array, built from the batch block below.
Element ids are bounded integers and never an enum. No string has a maxLength. A pattern uses explicit character ranges only, because Ollama reads "." as any character.
aliases are the other names a model uses for the verb. An alias must be unique, and it must not be the name of a verb.

verbs.name: type
verbs.prompt: type {element_id, text, submit} - replace the text in field [element_id]; submit true presses Enter after typing

verbs.name: press_key
verbs.prompt: press_key {key} - press one key: Enter, Escape, Tab, ArrowDown, ArrowUp, ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, PageDown, PageUp, Home, End, Backspace, Delete

verbs.name: navigate
verbs.prompt: navigate {url} - open a full https:// URL in this tab

verbs.name: go_back
verbs.prompt: go_back {} - go back in the browser history

verbs.name: go_forward
verbs.prompt: go_forward {} - go forward in the browser history

verbs.name: read_page_text
verbs.prompt: read_page_text {} - read more text of this page

verbs.name: execute_js
verbs.prompt: execute_js {code} - run JavaScript in the page and get the value it returns

verbs.name: read_network_requests
verbs.prompt: read_network_requests {filter, includeBody, limit} - see the recent network requests of this page; every field is optional

verbs.name: browser_batch
verbs.prompt: browser_batch {steps, stopOnError} - run up to 8 steps on this page in one reply; each step is a click, type, scroll, press_key or wait action with its own fields

verbs.name: wait
verbs.prompt: wait {amount} - wait 1 to 5 seconds, only while the page is still loading

verbs.name: finish
verbs.prompt: finish {answer} - the task is done; answer is the full answer for the user

verbs.name: ask_user
verbs.prompt: ask_user {question} - ask the user, only if you cannot go on without them

verbs.name: open_window
verbs.prompt: open_window {url} - open a new browser window (rare; use navigate for a new page)
